features.text: The patient is 44 years old and female.
The patient has had left shoulder pain for about a week.
The left shoulder pain started after a gymnastics class where the patient may have fallen into a weird position during a move.
The left shoulder pain is severe and occurs with any movement of the left shoulder.
The patient has not taken any pain medication except for Tylenol for a couple of days, but it did not help.
The patient has not noticed any swelling, bruising, or numbness/tingling in the left arm or hand since the injury.
The patient has not experienced any clicking, locking, or weakness in the left shoulder since the injury.
The patient has not experienced any radiating pain to the arm or neck.
The patient has not experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in the left arm or hand since the injury.
The patient has not had any prior imaging or evaluation of the left shoulder, such as X-rays or MRI.
The patient has no history of shoulder dislocations or labral tears.
The patient has difficulty sleeping on the affected side due to pain.
The patient has noticed a limitation in the ability to lift the left arm or perform daily activities with the left hand.
The patient describes the injury as occurring during a gymnastics move where they toppled over into a weird position, possibly going overboard.
